evidence: Jetz & Pyron 2018: ten 1,000-tree files of taxonomically complete dated trees (vertlife GCS amph_shl_new_Posterior_7238.1000-10000.trees.zip, md5 c6f1f27d1ffef5e764ba0d5af45dac2c; also Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.cc3n6j5), already thinned samples, so no burn-in; outgroup Homo sapiens stated by the source (main text p.856). Not distributed with the atlas (1.4 GB); measured on whitebox.

McTavish et al. 2025: 100 trees, each node dated by a randomly drawn published date with stochastic taxon addition; input intervals are not propagated and about 40% of nodes are interpolated (Methods, 'Estimating dates'). Recorded to show why no interval is counted.

Bechteler et al. 2023: 1,000 bootstrap trees each dated with treePL under the same calibrations (Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.3j9kd51qm); the root carries a 515 Ma maximum constraint, so its spread is expected to be nil.

Basava 2024 BEAST2 tree log (github.com/kcbasava/ceph-brain-evolution phylogeny/BEAUti_nov28-tree.trees), 10,001 states starting at state 0: a raw MCMC log, so the first 10% is dropped, TreeAnnotator's default; no outgroup (root = Coleoidea).

Vaga et al. 2025 BEAST2 MCC tree annotated by TreeAnnotator (Figshare doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.29242487, scle.mcc.mean.nex). The study's ingroup is Scleractinia; its 17 antipatharian and corallimorpharian outgroups are Cnidaria, so D7 keeps them in the canonical file, and they are excluded only from crown-node extraction (D21; list in Data/raw/revision-2026-10/cnidaria/outside_focal_clade_scleractinia.txt). The focal node is crown Scleractinia.

Nakov, Beaulieu & Alverson 2018 (Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.583628): 1,001 treePL chronograms under the same calibrations, tree 1 the best ML tree (the canonical source) and 1,000 bootstrap trees; outside = the 20 non-diatom stramenopile outgroups pruned by D7. The diatom crown carries a 190 Ma minimum calibration (cfile-batch).
Mongiardino Koch et al. 2022 PhyloBayes chronogram: every internal node carries an 'upper_lower' label; read from the shipped canonical file, whose root after D7 pruning is the echinoderm crown.

Rabosky et al. 2018 100 all-taxon-assembled trees: one treePL backbone with taxonomically placed species added by TACT per tree; fishtreeoflife.org states these trees should generally not be used for trait evolution. Recorded to show why no interval is counted.

Zapata et al. 2014 MCMCTree chronogram (Figure 4; bitbucket caseywdunn/gastropoda at ad4d39f) with a 95% interval on every node, time unit 100 Myr; outside = the 14 non-gastropod molluscs pruned by D7 (labels as written in the deposit).
Upham et al. 2019 NDexp MCC tree annotated by TreeAnnotator (Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.tb03d03), identical to the canonical source; outgroup Anolis carolinensis stated by the source.

Stein et al. 2018 1-fossil scenario: 10,000 trees = 500 treePL datings of one fixed RAxML topology under root ages drawn from the lognormal calibration density x 20 polytomy resolutions (accepted MS pp.16-18); the spread is the sampled calibration density, not a data-derived posterior. The root calibration is a lognormal density between a hard minimum of 333.56 Myr and a soft maximum of 422.4 Myr with its midpoint at 377.98 Myr (accepted MS p.16, Data/raw/revision-2026-10/sharks/stein2018_accepted_ms_summit_sfu.pdf); the source summarised the set by TreeAnnotator median node heights (p.17).
Lavrov et al. 2023 PhyloBayes chronogram: every internal node carries an 'upper_lower' label; read from the shipped canonical file (no tip pruned).

Tonini et al. 2016: ten 1,000-tree files of taxonomically complete dated trees (vertlife GCS squamatetree/squam_shl_new_Posterior_9755.1000-10000.trees.zip, md5 base64 LZkEkkKxn8+3KcZh0Wxh4A== as listed by the bucket, fetched 2026-10-08; the same ten files are on Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.db005, whose API returned 401), already thinned samples, so no burn-in, as for Amphibians; outgroup Sphenodon punctatus, pruned by D7, so the focal node is crown Squamata. Not distributed with the atlas (1.9 GB).
Thomson et al. 2021 BEAST MCC tree bd.mcc.median_heights.tre (Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.jh9w0vt8w), the canonical source; outgroups Alligator and Gallus stated by the source (p.6).
